title: Public demonstration of recording and Because They All Love You
summary: The Gennett company sets up its equipment in a Cincinnati auditorium and broadcasts; Davison later spent thirty years finding that record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yes and I remember once during -- we went into a big -- they wanted the Gennett Company to show the public how records were made and, so, they took all that equipment, which is unbelievable how they did this -- they took all that heavy equipment out of there and put it on a bandstand in a big auditorium in the center of Cincinnati---
Yeah--- about from Richmond from Cincinnati---
Yeah and set it up and it was broadcasted - the same time over the air and 5,000 people stood there listening to us without anybody even coughing or making a sound.
They were afraid to ruin the record---

No, but they--- but you could, very easily. You know, just ruin the whole thing. And, we made one song that day - it was called, "Because They All Love You" and I took a little jazz course on that ---I tried to get that record; I think I was 30 years trying to find that record--- I finally got it.
